title: MATHREAL: We Keep It Real! A Real Scene Benchmark for Evaluating Math Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper introduces MATHREAL, a benchmark dataset for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on math reasoning tasks using real-world photographs of K–12 math questions. The authors argue that existing multimodal math benchmarks rely mostly on clean, processed images and therefore do not reflect authentic school-related usage, where students may photograph textbook pages, worksheets, or homework with mobile phones under noisy real-world conditions. The paper focuses on the problem of whether current MLLMs can robustly perceive and solve visual math problems when images contain blur, glare, perspective distortion, handwritten marks, and other common artifacts.

The approach is the construction and evaluation of a 2,000-item benchmark of photographed K–12 math questions sourced from authentic educational materials. The dataset includes questions across elementary, middle school, and high school levels, with categories such as geometry, logical reasoning, function graphs, and statistical charts. Each item is manually annotated with ground-truth question text, figure descriptions, answers, and labels for 14 types of real-world visual interference. The authors then evaluate multiple closed and open-source multimodal models under several input conditions, including image-only input and settings with human-annotated or model-generated text/diagram descriptions, to separate perception from reasoning challenges.

The context is K–12 educational use, especially student-facing scenarios in which learners use handheld mobile devices to capture math questions from textbooks, exams, and printed exercises. Although the paper references real educational settings, it is not an intervention study in classrooms and does not test learning outcomes or causal effects on students. Instead, it evaluates AI model performance on benchmark tasks derived from school materials.

The main conclusion is that current MLLMs perform much worse on realistic educational images than on cleaner benchmark inputs, showing substantial weaknesses in OCR, figure perception, and mathematical reasoning under noisy conditions. Even the best-performing model achieved only modest accuracy on the benchmark. The authors conclude that real-world educational deployment requires more robust visual perception and reasoning capabilities, and that MATHREAL provides a more realistic testbed for diagnosing these limitations. For the targeted verification topic of generative AI and foundational reading outcomes, this paper is a clear negative finding / near-miss: it concerns generative AI evaluation in K–12, but only for mathematical reasoning benchmarks, not reading interventions or causal evidence on foundational literacy outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark/dataset paper evaluating multimodal large language models on photographed K-12 math problems, not an education intervention study. It provides no causal design, no student learning experiment, and no direct K-12 evidence on foundational reading or literacy outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact on learners is estimated because the paper reports model benchmark accuracy rather than effects on student outcomes. It is therefore not evidence of impact for generative AI on foundational reading in K-12 settings.
